cards.explanation: The answer is three, friends. Deuteronomy 19:2 says Israel is to set apart three cities within the land the LORD is giving them. I can barely keep three cookie trays straight when the timer goes off, so I respect it. Small number, big job, and the next verses show what the job is.

The answer is so any manslayer can flee to them, friends. Deuteronomy 19:3 says to build roads and divide the land into three regions "…so that any manslayer can flee to these cities." The roads are there so the cities can actually be reached. A refuge nobody can get to is just a nice view.

The answer is one who killed his neighbor by accident, friends. Deuteronomy 19:4 says he killed his neighbor accidentally, without intending to harm him. That detail carries the whole teaching. Hold onto it, because the passage comes back to a very different kind of case.

The answer is that the blade flies off the handle, friends. Deuteronomy 19:5 says he swings his axe to chop down a tree, but the blade flies off the handle and strikes and kills his neighbor. It's a sad, sudden moment, and I think that's why the example sticks. It shows what accidentally really looks like.

The answer is that the avenger of blood might chase him down, friends. Deuteronomy 19:6 says the avenger of blood might pursue the manslayer in a rage and strike him dead. The city gives him somewhere to run to. Without one, the danger follows him down the road.

The answer is False, friends. Deuteronomy 19:6 says the avenger might strike him dead "…though he did not deserve to die, since he did not intend any harm." This man didn't mean it. That's why the passage gives him a place to run.

The answer is True, friends. Deuteronomy 19:9 says that if the LORD gives Israel all the land He promised, and if they carefully keep all these commandments, loving the LORD their God and walking in His ways at all times, then they are to add three more cities to these three. So there are conditions, and the land is only one of them. That makes six cities in all.

The answer is True, friends. Deuteronomy 19:9 says this comes "…if you carefully keep all these commandments I am giving you today, loving the LORD your God and walking in His ways at all times…" Then comes the command to add three more cities. The keeping and the loving are right there in the sentence.

The answer is innocent, friends. Deuteronomy 19:10 says "Thus innocent blood will not be shed in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance…" It also adds, "…so that you will not be guilty of bloodshed." The cities are there to protect people who didn't deserve to die.

The answer is that the elders bring him back to the avenger of blood, friends. Deuteronomy 19:12 says the elders of his city must send for him, bring him back, and hand him over to the avenger of blood to die. This is the man from verse 11 who hates his neighbor and lies in wait. So no city shelters him. The shelter in verses 4 to 6 was for the man who killed by accident.

The answer is False, friends. Deuteronomy 19:13 says, "You must show him no pity." It also says Israel is to purge the guilt of shedding innocent blood. Mercy for the accidental case, no pity for the planned one.

The answer is move, friends. Deuteronomy 19:14 says, "You must not move your neighbor’s boundary marker…" Those markers were set up by their ancestors to mark the inheritance. I think it's like nudging the property line over a little at night and hoping nobody checks. Nobody should get away with that, and the verse says don't.

The answer is two or three, friends. Deuteronomy 19:15 says a matter "…must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses." One lone voice isn't enough. It takes more than one person saying so.

The answer is False, friends. Deuteronomy 19:17 says both parties to the dispute must stand in the presence of the LORD. They stand before the priests and judges in office at that time. The accuser has to stand there too.

The answer is that the judges investigate thoroughly, friends. Deuteronomy 19:18 says, "The judges shall investigate thoroughly…" They don't just take someone's word for it. Thorough means checking, then checking again.

The answer is to do to him what he intended for his brother, friends. Deuteronomy 19:19 says, "…you must do to him as he intended to do to his brother." The liar gets what he planned for the man he accused. The text says this is how Israel purges the evil from among them.

The answer is afraid, friends. Deuteronomy 19:20 says, "Then the rest of the people will hear and be afraid…" Word gets around. When people hear what happened to a liar, I think they'll think twice before trying it.

The answer is True, friends. Deuteronomy 19:20 says the people "…will never again do anything so evil among you." That's what Moses, Israel's leader, tells them will follow. The words are right there in the verse.
